newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: IMF team begins talks for new loan to Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: IMF team begins talks for new loan to Pakistan.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund team began talks with Pakistani government officials on Thursday for a new medium-term loan to support Islamabad's structural reforms, a government official said.

The Finance Ministry official said the IMF team, which arrived in Islamabad on Wednesday, would continue technical discussions next week before starting policy talks on July 21 for an enhanced structural adjustment facility (ESAF).

Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz had said this week that the talks would result in a new loan for Pakistan because the governemnt of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif had already undertaken structural reforms ahead of the IMF's initial expectations.

Pakistan's reforms in the past four months included drastic tax and tariff cuts, reforms in the banking sector and tax collecting administration, and a review of governmental machinery and downsizing of public corporations.

Pakistani officials say the revenue and spending targets laid out in the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) were generally consistent with the reform programme, but some fine-tuning might be needed.
It is up to the IMF board to determine the size of any new loan, but Pakistan expects it to be around $1.2 billion.

Pakistan signed a $1.5 billion, three-year ESAF lending programme with the IMF in February 1994, but the IMF halted disbursements after the former government led by Benazir Bhutto announced a 1995/96 budget that failed to meet agreed targets.
A balance-of-payments crisis in October 1995 forced the Bhutto government to seek an IMF standby loan, which was suspended in March last year, again because of missed targets.

The standby was resumed and expanded in December after a caretaker government took over from the dismissed Bhutto, but the IMF halted it in March when Sharif's government said the targets were out of reach.
At that time the IMF welcomed Sharif's plans for structural reform, including tax reform and tax administration reform, faster privatisation, and revival of industry and farming.
